title: Test-Time Backdoor Detection for Object Detection Models (TRACE), CVPR 2025
claim: Two observations: poisoned samples are MORE consistent across varied backgrounds; clean samples are more consistent under different focal information. Method applies foreground AND background transformations and measures variance in object confidence.
reported_result: ~30% AUROC improvement over SOTA; resistant to adaptive attacks
relevance: Our trace_ctc implements only the background arm. TRACE's second observation implies a foreground arm with an INVERTED direction.
proposed_change: Add a foreground/focal transformation arm whose statistic is confidence variance (high = suspicious), the mirror of the background arm, and fuse the two.
measured_here: not measured. Our background arm reads AUROC 0.816 on the null control, i.e. it is partly responding to the stamp

title: Detecting Backdoors in Object Detection via Pre-NMS Prediction Distribution Shift (DistScan)
claim: Backdoor injection systematically shifts a model's PRE-NMS prediction class distribution away from its training class frequencies, even on clean inputs with no trigger present. Flag via JS divergence.
reported_result: 96.99% average detection accuracy on 288 models (YOLOv5 and Faster R-CNN, COCO and VOC, three scene-level attacks); +27.32pp over the best applicable baseline
relevance: Structurally immune to the contamination that forced a placebo arm everywhere else here: it never stamps a trigger, so it cannot be measuring the ink.
proposed_change: Implement pre-NMS class-prior divergence as an asset-level signal and calibrate its threshold on clean models.
measured_here: ADOPTED and measured on runs/day1 (40 clean images per model, conf gate 0.5, each model's own CLEAN training class frequencies as reference). Clean null mean JS 0.0677, max 0.1876. AUROC clean-vs-kind: gma 0.800, rma 0.573, ood_insert 0.564, oda 0.554, dup_flood 0.509, oga 0.496, label_flip 0.464. So it separates gma only -- and gma is the ONLY attack that the independent placebo-controlled test also says implanted. Convergent evidence from two unrelated methods. The null is too wide to use as a general detector at this sample size.

title: E-SHIFT: Anytime-valid sequential hypothesis testing for distribution shift
claim: An e-value is a one-observation test statistic; an e-process gives anytime-valid monitoring so continuous peeking does not inflate the error rate.
relevance: Our drift module decides on a fixed-sample p-value and MONITOR/RE-ATTEST re-checks it on a stream.
proposed_change: Replace the repeated fixed-sample test with a precommitted e-process/wealth ledger and an optional-stopping-safe alarm; calibrate bets under the declared null only.

title: Detector Collapse: scene-level backdoor (cited in DistScan, ref [12])
claim: A single trigger induces all three effects (misclassification, disappearance, insertion) across every object in the scene, and is explicitly designed to be position-independent and to have no specific victim-target class correspondence.
reported_result: defeats ODSCAN and MIA, the prior object-detection detectors
relevance: Three of four trigger attacks here never implanted under placebo control. gma (global misclassification) is the only positive, and it is the closest thing in our taxonomy to a scene-level attack.
proposed_change: Add a scene-level attack recipe to the corpus as a candidate implantable positive, and verify it under the placebo criterion before scoring any detector against it.

title: Trigger implantation search: rate 0.5, six recipes, six seeds, placebo-controlled
claim: Measured here, not from a paper: the shipped high-salience patch cannot implant an object-generation backdoor because a clean model already calls a checkerboard an object, so the poisoning asks the model to do what it already does.
reported_result: net ASR (placebo-controlled, null-subtracted) mean / max, and usable models out of 6: gma patch on_object 0.308/0.625, 1/6; oga blended 0.315/0.525, 1/6; gma patch fixed 0.268/0.456, 0/6; rma blended 0.143/0.273, 0/6; oda blended 0.000/0.000, 0/6; oga patch fixed 0.000/0.000, 0/6
relevance: Three of four trigger attacks were unusable at the shipped recipes. Raising the poisoning rate to 0.5 makes exactly one family usable, and only on a minority of seeds, so the trigger axis of the corpus needs many seeds rather than a better recipe.
proposed_change: Adopt oga+blended at rate 0.5 as the primary object-generation recipe and scale the seed count (a ~17% usable rate needs ~30 seeds for 5 positives); mark oda as not covered; drop the high-salience patch for generation attacks. Separately test the scene-level attack from the ledger as a candidate for the disappearance cell.
